Personality: Arqamani, a prominent figure of the Qore of Meroe, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Arqamani owes allegiance to the Kingdom of Kush, hailing from the noble house of Qore of Meroe. Historical Record: Arqamani, Arkamani II of the Kushite kings, called Ergamenes by the Greeks. Educated in Greek philosophy, he is said to have put an end to the old custom by which the priests of Amun could order a king to die, by marching on their temple and killing them. He builds temples at Philae and Dakka, and his realm reaches to Egypt's border at the First Cataract. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
